title: What is GTD?
supports: David Allen's five steps: capture, clarify (decide if actionable, define the next action and project), organize, reflect (review frequently), engage.

title: Maker's Schedule, Manager's Schedule
supports: July 2009 essay: makers need half-day blocks, managers work in hourly slots; one meeting can break a maker's afternoon; cluster meetings at the end of the day (office hours).

title: Books
supports: Deep Work (2016), A World Without Email (2021) on communication overload, Slow Productivity (2024), and the Time-Block Planner.

title: Steven Rogelberg
supports: Author of The Surprising Science of Meetings and Glad We Met (one-on-one meetings); evidence-based approach to making meetings efficient, engaging and inclusive.

title: 2017 Letter to Shareholders
supports: Amazon uses narratively structured six-page memos instead of slides, read silently at the start of each meeting; a great memo may take a week or more and is rewritten with colleagues' help.

title: Breaking down the infinite workday (Work Trend Index special report)
supports: 17 June 2025; Microsoft 365 telemetry to 15 February 2025 plus a 31,000-person survey: 117 emails a day, most skimmed in under 60 seconds; 153 Teams messages a weekday; an interruption every 2 minutes in core hours; meetings after 8 pm up 16%; 57% of meetings ad hoc.

title: Plain language guide
supports: Official US plain language guidance: principles, writing for your audience, the Plain Writing Act of 2010, designing and testing for understanding.

title: Voice and tone
supports: Voice stays the same while tone changes with the reader and situation; consider the reader's state of mind; clarity over entertainment.

title: Delegate and collaborate on email
supports: Delegates can read, send and delete mail but cannot change the password or account settings or chat; up to 10 delegates on personal accounts and 1,000 on work accounts; admin must allow it; sent mail shows the delegate's address.

title: Allow someone else to manage your mail and calendar
supports: Outlook delegate levels Reviewer, Author and Editor; scope from calendar only to the whole mailbox; send as can only be set by an admin; work or school accounts only; delegates can use Copilot on items they can access.

title: Use Google Workspace connectors
supports: Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors: search, read and draft; sending, sharing, moving and trashing need approval by default; existing Google permissions apply; Team and Enterprise owners must enable them.

title: Take notes for me in Google Meet
supports: AI notes saved to the organiser's Drive and attached to the Calendar event; all participants are notified; host controls; eight spoken languages, one per meeting; summaries may be incomplete or inaccurate; needs an eligible Workspace edition or Google AI plan.

title: Using Meeting Summary with Zoom AI
supports: Host or co-host starts the AI meeting summary on eligible paid plans; an icon shows AI features are active; summaries go by email to those the host chooses and appear in Zoom Hub. No date on the page.

title: 2025 IC3 Annual Report (Internet Crime Report)
supports: 2025: 1,008,597 complaints and $20.877 billion reported losses; business email compromise losses $3,046,598,558 (2024: $2,770,151,146); over $30 million in BEC losses involved AI; April 2025 case where an Oregon city office's $6 million wire was recalled. PDF opened and converted to text.

title: Avoiding and Reporting Gift Card Scams
supports: No real business or government agency will ever tell you to buy a gift card to pay them; contact the card company fast and report at ReportFraud.ftc.gov. Dated July 2023.

title: How long should I keep records?
supports: General 3-year rule, 6 and 7-year cases, employment tax records at least 4 years, indefinitely if no return filed; page reviewed 30 June 2026.

title: Running a limited company: company and accounting records
supports: UK companies keep records about the company (shareholders, votes and resolutions) and accounting records, generally for 6 years from the end of the last financial year they relate to, longer in some cases.

title: Foreign travel advice
supports: Country-by-country advice on entry requirements, safety and security, health and local laws for about 226 destinations, with email alerts.

title: Apply for an electronic travel authorisation (ETA)
supports: Most visitors from Europe, the USA, Australia, Canada and certain other countries need an ETA instead of a visa, including transit through UK border control; each traveller needs one; British and Irish passport holders do not.

title: Using Credit Cards and Disputing Charges
supports: Fair Credit Billing Act: dispute letter must reach the card issuer within 60 days after the first bill showing the error; issuer acknowledges within 30 days and resolves within 90 days; write to the billing-inquiries address. Dated May 2022.

title: How to complain
supports: Complain to the financial business first; it has up to 8 weeks for a final response (15 days for payment services and e-money); bring the complaint to the ombudsman within 6 months of the final response; free.

title: Accepting returns and giving refunds
supports: UK: faulty goods must be refunded, repaired or replaced; 6-month presumption; up to 6 years to claim (5 in Scotland); online purchases can be cancelled within 14 days of receipt, refund within 14 days of getting the item back.

title: Guarantees and returns: legal guarantee
supports: EU minimum 2-year legal guarantee; repair or replacement first, then refund; defects within 1 year (2 in some countries) presumed present at delivery; commercial guarantees cannot reduce legal rights. Last checked by the EU 5 October 2026.

title: Cancelling or returning goods bought online
supports: EU 14-day cooling-off period for distance purchases from delivery (goods) or contract (services); exceptions such as personalised or perishable goods and dated tickets; who pays return postage. Last checked by the EU 28 April 2026.
